title: Value vs Reference Types in Swift

scenes.say: Ever wonder why Swift has both structs and classes? Let's see why this difference matters for your code.

scenes.label: Struct
scenes.sub: Value type: copied when assigned or passed
scenes.say: A struct in Swift is a value type. That means when you assign or pass it, you get a fresh copy.

scenes.label: Class
scenes.sub: Reference type: points to same instance
scenes.say: A class, on the other hand, is a reference type. Assign it, and you just point to the same instance in memory.
Here, changing b does not change a. Each variable owns its own copy, so no surprises.
With structs, you avoid hidden side effects and get thread safety by default. Classes share state, so changes can leak across your app.

scenes.question: Can structs inherit from other structs?
scenes.right: Nope—only classes support inheritance in Swift.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: only classes support inheritance in Swift. Structs can't inherit from other structs.
